title.narrative: PPDP Youth employment- RUTA MOTOR Colombia 2018-2026

description.narrative: Projektet Ruta Motor är den andra fasen av ett program som har fått stöd från Sida sedan november 2014 med genomförandepartnern Neme Foundation (tidigare stöd: 55190001). Detta projektstöd syftar till att bryta den generationsöverskridande fattigdomscykeln för unga utsatta människor genom ett offentlig-privat partnerskap som tillhandahåller relevant arbetskraft till marknaden. De tre avsedda resultaten är följande: (i) Förbättra anställningsvillkoren för 1 000 utsatta unga män och kvinnor från Bogotá, Medellin, Cali och Valledupar; (ii) Förbättra de privata företagens deltagande och deras samordning med relevanta offentliga institutioner; och (iii) Stärka det offentliga utbudet av yrkesutbildning och högre utbildning som svarar mot efterfrågan på arbetskraft. Detta program bidrar också till FN:s säkerhetsråds resolution 2250/2015 eftersom det syftar till att förebygga att unga människor drabbas av effekterna av konflikter, inklusive förflyttning, och förhindra att de ansluter sig till väpnade grupper.

The project Ruta Motor is the second phase of a programme that has been supported by Sida since November 2014 with the implementing partner Neme Foundation (previous contribution: 55190001). This project support aims at breaking the inter-generational cycle of poverty for young vulnerable people through a public private partnership that provides relevant labour force to the market. The three intended outputs are: (i) Improving conditions for employment of 1000 vulnerable young men and women from Bogotá, Medellin, Cali, and Valledupar; (ii) Improving participation of private companies and their coordination with relevant public institutions; and (iii) Strengthen the public offer of vocational training and higher education that responds to the labour demand. This programme also contributes to the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2250/2015 as it aims to prevent young people from the effects of conflict, including displacement, and prevent their connection with armed groups.

This contribution aims in the long term at breaking the inter-generational cycle of poverty for young vulnerable people through a public private partnership that provide relevant labor force to the market. The three intended outputs are, first, improving conditions for employment of 1000 vulnerable young men and women from Bogota, Medellin, Cali and Valledupar; second, improving participation of private companies and their coordination with relevant public institutions and, finally, to strengthen the public offer of vocational training and higher education in order that responds to the labor demand.

Regarding the young participants, as of 2024, groups 2.6 and 2.7 were still active and progressing through various stages of the project. The Neme Foundation also included two additional groups of participants, groups 2.8 and 2.9. As of December 31, 2024, a total of 952 young people from Ruta Motor 2.0, 2.5, and 2.6 had completed the productive phase of the program. Of these, 711 were from Groups 2.0, 211 from group 2.5, and 30 were from Cohort 2.6. 230 participants of groups 2.6 and 2.7 remain active in the program. The employment rate has varied among the groups: 2.0: 49%; 2.5: 67%; 2.6: 60%. The lowest employment rate was due to the pandemic and afterwards this rate has risen, achieving the expected result of at least 60%. The gender issue has been raised during the whole activity period. Over time the project has in practice become more feminine with the change of demand from companies for more administrative rather than mechanic training, with the exception of group 2.6 that was a specific training for a mining company. This project is therefore a great opportunity for Sida´s pilot of Womens Economic Empowerment.
In 2024, the Neme Foundation partnered with General Motors (GM) to conduct a pilot project in Bogotá, called "Connect Your Future", group 2.8. The project provided 35 young, certified electricians with the opportunity to expand their knowledge of automotive electricity through additional training. The project aimed to develop a talent pool for the future of the automotive sector and GM. It aligned with General Motors' global environmental vision of facilitating the transition from fossil fuels to zero-emission technologies.
Additionally, in April 2024, due to the positive results obtained in Ruta Motor, CHM Minería requested the opening of a new group, Ruta Motor 2.9. In August, 50 young people began technical training in a program called "Maintenance of Heavy Equipment for Infrastructure, Mining, and Transportation, of which 25 are studying in Cesar and the other 25 are studying in La Guajira. In addition, in 2024, a total of 161 young people participated in supplemental courses. Of those, 155 were in cohort 2.7 and received training in various subjects, such as languages, Excel, and financial education. Similarly, four young people from group 2.6 completed a driving course, and one received crane operator training.
The graduation ceremonies for cohorts 2.6 and 2.8 of Ruta Motor took place in November 2024. Cohort 2.6 celebrated in La Jagua de Ibirico, Valledupar, and Cohort 2.8 celebrated in Bogotá at the Central Technical Institute (ETIC) with the Embassy´s participation.
Various outcome and impact evaluations were conducted to show the results obtained in the first cohort of Ruta Motor, the midterm and final evaluations of 963 young people in Ruta Motor 2.0, and the midterm and final evaluations of young people in Ruta Motor 2.5. Results of these evaluations were included in previous statements and conclusion on performance. It was agreed that no further impact evaluations would be conducted for groups 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, and 2.9, but rather, focus groups would be held to gain a more holistic view of the results obtained. In 2024 focal group were held to evaluate group 2.6: the conclusion was that The Ruta Motor program has proven to be an effective tool for developing the soft skills and competencies of its participants. This approach is crucial for strengthening self-esteem and empowerment, which are determining factors that allow participants to face workplace and academic challenges with greater confidence. The program is a turning point in the training and personal development of young people, preparing them to face life's challenges with greater resilience. Furthermore, the program promotes the employability of graduates through strategic alliances with companies. This provides them with the practical tools necessary to improve their quality of life and renews their hope for a brighter future for themselves and their families. The only recommendation was to implement complementary activities, such as periodic field trips, for the nine-month academic stage in which participants dedicate themselves to studying. These visits would familiarize young people with the professional environment they will enter, strengthening their preparation and facilitating a more effective transition.
Secondly, in order to increase the commitment of private companies, Neme foundation reported a progress of 95% of the expected final goal. For instance, the group 2.8 and the connect your future program in alliance with General Motors, also promoted exchange with other companies of the Group A, promoting training in sustainability and the transition to zero-emission technologies. These visits also created future job opportunities for the participants. ENEL (multinational in the energy sector) also participated in the initiative by contributing its expertise in electric vehicle chargers. However, while advancing the implementation of Connect Your Future, in 2024, the Colmotores plant in Bogotá closed after 62 years of operation. This was a hard blow for the project participants, who had hoped to engage more with the employees and processes of the plant. Nevertheless, the Neme Foundation organized visits to other companies to reinforce the project's practical and interactive tools.
Finaly, regarding the public sector, the Neme Foundation participated in launching the Labor Ecosystem Viewer, an initiative of the Secretariat of Social Integration in collaboration with the Public Employment Service. The Foundation also attended follow-up meetings and monitored the tool to help the project's young people find job opportunities. Although the agreement with SENA ended in 2022, collaboration continued without an agreement.
